archetypes.name: doc-surface-sync
archetypes.rationale: The plan lists a grep scope for stale 'No-auto-apply' prose but does not confirm that scope is exhaustive against the actual repo; a missed doc surface leaves a contradictory invariant in production.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read the actual files that could contain Gate B behavioral statements: docs/workflow-lifecycle.md, SECURITY.md, skills/design/SKILL.md, skills/design/references/approval-gates.md, README.md, and any .claude/rules/ files that reference /design or Gate B. Check whether the plan's grep list ('No-auto-apply', 'never auto-revise', 'plan is never auto-revised', 'auto-apply') covers every match in those files, and identify any doc surfaces the plan omits from its reconciliation scope. Flag stale invariant language that the plan would leave contradicted. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: run-params-parity
archetypes.rationale: The plan claims byte-for-byte parity with the brainstorm/partition precedent in write-run-params.sh and test-write-run-params.sh, but also relies on test-design-structure.sh not pinning the flag list or run-params schema — those pins are speculative ('likely') and not verified against the actual file.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/write-run-params.sh and scripts/test-write-run-params.sh to verify that the plan's proposed diff (adding --manual-gate-b, require_enum, jq --arg, and four test cases) aligns with how --brainstorm-requested and --partition-requested are currently implemented. Also read scripts/test-design-structure.sh to determine whether it pins the public flag list, run-params.json field names, or Gate B option count — the plan says 'likely' but does not confirm. Identify any structural anchor pins the plan fails to enumerate for update. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: apply-body-factoring
archetypes.rationale: The plan's 'branch-and-reuse' claim relies on both auto-apply and manual-mode option (a) referencing a shared Apply-all body subsection in approval-gates.md, but the plan prose sometimes describes adding new body text rather than factoring — leaving room for silent copy-paste divergence that skips dedup-sweep or EMIT_PLAN on the auto-apply path.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read skills/design/references/approval-gates.md to map the current Apply-all body: its exact steps, ordering, and any anchor strings. Cross-check whether the plan specifies a named shared subsection or merely says 'run existing Apply-all body verbatim' without a concrete refactor target. Determine whether the plan's auto-apply path description in the approval-gates.md section could be implemented as a copy-paste of the manual-mode body rather than a true shared reference, and flag any wording that would allow the dedup-sweep, ACTION=EMIT_PLAN, validator invocation, or Step 2b.5 call to be omitted from the auto-apply branch without detection. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
